channel.description: Latest articles from CT News Junkie (ctnewsjunkie.com)

item.title: Podcast | Talking Mattresses With The Mattress Recycling Council Of Connecticut
item.description: We sleep on one every night and hope to get a good night's sleep from our mattresses. But what happens to them after they come to the end of their useful life? You might be surprised to find out.

item.title: CT’s Community Health Centers Seek To Limit Coverage Losses From Federal Changes
item.description: “Community health centers are on the front lines of keeping Connecticut residents healthy, insured and connected to care,” said Shawn K. Frick, CEO of CHC/ACT. “As major changes to Medicaid and other health programs are implemented, the state must invest now in the systems, workforce and community-based supports that make access to care possible.”

item.title: Senate Democrats Eye CT Sales Tax Cuts, Renters’ Tax Credits As Part Of Affordability Measures
item.description: Senate President Martin Looney of New Haven said the federal tariffs and cuts to healthcare subsidies had caused an affordability crisis. S.B. 1, he said, “provides relief where families need it most, cutting taxes on clothing, school supplies, and groceries while providing tax credits for those caring for elderly or disabled relatives."

item.title: Lamont: Prepare For Blizzard Conditions
item.description: The National Weather Service defines a blizzard as a storm containing heavy or blowing snow with winds in excess of 35 miles per hour for at least three hours and visibilities frequently less than a quarter mile.

item.title: Lamont Declares State Of Emergency, Bans Commercial Vehicles From Highways At 5pm Sunday
item.description: The emergency order is being implemented in coordination with Connecticut’s neighboring states, which are also issuing their own similar emergency orders in response to the storm as it is expected to impact the entire northeast region.

item.title: Analysis | Advice To CT’s Next Medicaid Director
item.description: Healthcare analyst Ellen Andrews has some advice for the state's next Medicaid Director.

item.title: The Supreme Court Struck Down Some Of Trump’s Tariffs, But Impact On CT Is Unclear, Experts Say
item.description: In a 6-3 ruling, the justices struck down about half of Trump’s tariffs, ruling that the law that he based them on does not grant the right to implement them. But what does that mean for Connecticut businesses and residents?

item.title: Eversource, UI Report Thousands Without Power In CT Due To Storm
item.description: Nearly 20,000 customers of the state's major utilities providers are without power Monday morning, according to information from Eversource and United Illuminating co.

item.title: Adams & Knight Welcomes New VP Of Media
item.description: After a long hiatus we have rebooted the 210 Capitol Ave blog to keep you filled in on the various news items in the industries adjacent to politics and public policy. It's been a while but we'll get you caught up.

item.title: CT Officials Report 80 Crashes, 70mph Winds As Storm Winds Down
item.description: Connecticut State Police reported about 250 calls for vehicle assistance, mostly vehicles off the road. There also were multiple jackknifed tractor trailers, according to Sgt. Mike Hamill, in addition to 82 traffic accidents resulting in a pair of minor injuries.
